original: Generate a table for a byte-wise 32-bit CRC calculation on the polynomial: x^32+x^26+x^23+x^22+x^16+x^12+x^11+x^10+x^8+x^7+x^5+x^4+x^2+x+1. Polynomials over GF(2) are represented in binary, one bit per coefficient, with the lowest powers in the most significant bit. Then adding polynomials is just exclusive-or, and multiplying a polynomial by x is a right shift by one. If we call the above polynomial p, and represent a byte as the polynomial q, also with the lowest power in the most significant bit (so the byte 0xb1 is the polynomial x^7+x^3+x+1), then the CRC is (q*x^32) mod p, where a mod b

Polynomials sobre GF(2) sao representado em binario, um bit por coeficiente, com o mais baixo powers em the mais significativo bit. entao adicionando polynomials e apenas exclusivo-ou, and multiplicando a polynomial por x e a direito deslocamento por um. se nos chamar the acima polynomial p, and representa a byte como the polynomial q, tambem com o mais baixo energia em the mais significativo bit (so the byte 0xb1 e the polynomial x^7+x^3+x+1), entao the CRC e (q*x^32) mod p, onde a mod b
